title: Exponential Padding Preserves NP Membership
statement: Let $L$ and $V$ be languages of finite Boolean words, and let $C,c$ be natural numbers. Suppose $V$ belongs to $�\mathrm{P}$ and, for every word $x$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent to the existence of a word $u$ of length $C(2^{|x|+1})^c$ such that $xu\in V$. Then the language of pair encodings of $x$ with the all-ones word of length $C2^{(|x|+1)^c}$, for $x\in L$, belongs to $�\mathrm{NP}$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ and $V$ are languages of finite Boolean words
For every $x$, $x\in L$ iff there is $u$ with $|u|=C(2^{|x|+1})^c$ and $xu\in V$
replaced: Let $L$ and $V$ be languages with $V \in \mathrm{P}$, and let $C, c$ be natural numbers such that $x \in L$ if and only if some $u$ with $|u| = C \cdot 2^{(|x|+1)^c}$ has $x\,u \in V$. Then the exponentially padded language of $L$ belongs to $\mathrm{NP}$.
